title: phosphine oxides, P(O)H
activation: P-centred Pudovik carbonyl addition, proposed phospha-Brook rearrangement and β-fluoride elimination
endpoint: difluoromethyl, monofluoromethyl or methyl ketones; difluoroenol phosphinates
conditions: In the model reaction, Ph2P(O)H (1.2 equivalents), K2CO3 (2 equivalents), 1,4-dioxane, 80 °C, 6 h give difluoromethyl ketone in 80%; adding 4 Å molecular sieves affords difluoroenol phosphinate in 80%. Other endpoints require different reagent loading and temperature; see Section S2.5.
transfer_limits: RCOCF3 differs from RCOCH2CF3, and Ph2P(O)H differs from Ph2PH. The enol phosphinate contains C–O–P. Carbonyl interception and rearrangement are competing-pathway considerations, not direct failure of the project vinyl C–P endpoint.
source_location: L343 [2], DOI 10.1039/d5sc03915k; final primary article, Fig. 2A and Fig. 4; primary full text reviewed.
mechanistic_interpretation: Initial P-centred addition creates a C–P bond, followed by proposed phosphorus migration to oxygen and elimination. Product connectivity and endpoint must therefore be assessed after the whole sequence.

title: diphenyl diselenide as co-catalyst, not transferred Se partner
conditions: PC-I protocol, 1.2 equivalents azole, 5 mol% PhSeSePh and 5 mol% photocatalyst in DCE at 0.25 M under visible light. A separate PC-II protocol uses 3 mol% photocatalyst and toluene.
transfer_limits: Selenium functions as co-catalyst in a C-N forming route; this is not a C-Se monofluoroalkene precedent or a failed selenium donor test.
source_location: L347 [8], DOI 10.1039/d5sc04074d; primary full text, Table 1 and Scheme 2.
mechanistic_interpretation: The authors propose photocatalyst regeneration, deprotonation and hydrogen-atom transfer by selenium-derived species, selecting a CF2-retaining C–N endpoint. The source does not establish failed nucleophilic Se incorporation in the project system.
